subject: pharmacology
title: Bone, calcium and hypercalcaemia drugs

steps.tx: **Bisphosphonates** such as alendronate and zoledronate kill osteoclasts and strengthen bone, but oral tablets demand strict fasting and upright dosing with a full glass of water. Failure to stay upright for thirty to sixty minutes causes **oesophagitis**, and calcium with vitamin D must stay replete during therapy. Long treatment causes **osteonecrosis of the jaw** and atypical femoral fractures, so drug holidays follow prolonged use.
steps.say: Bisphosphonates strengthen bone by suppressing osteoclast activity over months of treatment. Oral tablets require fasting administration with a full glass of water. Patients remain upright afterwards because tablets otherwise burn the oesophagus severely. Long therapy rarely causes jaw necrosis and atypical thigh fractures.

steps.tx: **Denosumab** blocks RANKL every six months and suits chronic kidney disease because clinicians need no renal dose reduction for this antibody. Stopping treatment without follow on therapy causes **rebound vertebral fractures**, so transition to a bisphosphonate remains mandatory after discontinuation. **Teriparatide** builds new bone as an anabolic agent for severe osteoporosis but carries a two year lifetime limit, while raloxifene protects spine and lowers breast cancer risk.
steps.say: Denosumab blocks RANKL and strengthens bone with injections every six months. The antibody suits kidney disease because dosing requires no renal adjustment. Stopping treatment abruptly causes rebound vertebral fractures within months. Teriparatide builds new bone but treatment remains limited to two years.

steps.tx: The lateral spine radiograph shows **osteoporotic wedge fractures** where vertebral bodies lose anterior height and deform at the endplates under normal load. These silent fractures cause height loss and kyphosis and prove that bone strength has already failed, not merely thinned on a scan. The image explains why **antiresorptive therapy** and anabolic treatment aim to prevent the next fracture after the first **vertebral fracture** appears.
steps.say: The radiograph shows vertebral bodies collapsing anteriorly into wedge shapes under load. Osteoporotic fractures cause height loss, kyphosis and chronic back pain progressively. One vertebral fracture increases the risk of further fractures and requires effective bone treatment promptly. Antiresorptive therapy reduces the risk of subsequent fractures substantially.

steps.tx: **Hypercalcaemia** causes stones, bones, groans and psychiatric overtones with polyuria, constipation, confusion and a short QT interval on the electrocardiogram. Treatment starts with **saline diuresis first**, and loop diuretics follow only after volume repletion never before rehydration. **Bisphosphonates** lower calcium over days, calcitonin bridges the first hours, and steroids help granulomatous and lymphoma driven vitamin D mediated disease.
steps.say: Hypercalcaemia causes polyuria, constipation, confusion and abdominal pain in affected patients. Saline resuscitation starts treatment and restores circulating volume before other measures. Bisphosphonates lower calcium over days while calcitonin bridges the early hours. Steroids help when granulomas or lymphoma drive excess vitamin D activity.

vis.alt: Diagram showing hypercalcaemia symptoms (stones, bones, groans, psychiatric overtones) and initial treatment steps (saline diuresis, bisphosphonates, calcitonin).
vis.caption: Hypercalcaemia: symptoms and initial management

steps.tx: **Cinacalcet** acts as a calcimimetic for secondary hyperparathyroidism in dialysis patients and for parathyroid carcinoma when surgery cannot control calcium. Calcium and vitamin D underpin every osteoporosis regimen, with carbonate taken with meals and citrate preferred when gastric acid remains low. **Hypocalcaemia** causes Chvostek and Trousseau signs with prolonged QT, and intravenous **calcium gluconate** with cardiac monitoring treats severe symptomatic cases.
steps.say: Cinacalcet reduces parathyroid hormone and helps control calcium in dialysis patients with secondary hyperparathyroidism. Calcium and vitamin D support every osteoporosis regimen throughout treatment. Hypocalcaemia causes perioral tingling, carpopedal spasm and prolonged cardiac conduction. Intravenous calcium gluconate helps treat severe symptoms while clinicians check the heart and monitor conduction.
